TECHNICAL DESIGN DOCUMENT
Preserve semicolon-separated ATS link CC email addresses in UI and storage
Generated: 2026-10-21T10:01:37.094834+00:00
############################################################

1. SUMMARY
==========
In ATS Portal Service settings, the 'Enable Link to user placing order' CC Email Addresses field
does not retain semicolon separators after save and reload. The reported behavior is that values
entered as semicolon-separated are converted to comma-separated, unlike other CC email fields such
as Candidate Submitted Notifications. The issue is visible when a client administrator edits this
field, saves settings, and reloads the page.

2. REQUIREMENTS
===============
- When a client administrator enters multiple CC email addresses for
AtsIntegrationSettings.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses separated by semicolons, the saved
value must preserve semicolons so the UI can later display the same semicolon-separated string.
- The ATS integration UI field for sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses must no longer convert
semicolon-separated input to comma-separated on blur, save, or reload.
- Existing stored comma-separated values for
AtsIntegrationSettings.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses must remain readable and display
unchanged until the field is edited and saved again.
- Parsing of CC email addresses for downstream email sending must continue to accept both
semicolon-separated and comma-separated stored values.
- Behavior of other CC email fields, including Candidate Submitted Notifications fields represented
by CandidateDirectSettings and CustomRecipientList emailAddresses, must remain unchanged.
Non-functional:
- The fix must be limited to the ATS integration CC email field and must not change GraphQL schema
shapes for existing settings fields.
- Automated regression coverage must demonstrate that the current semicolon-to-comma conversion
fails before the fix and passes after it.

3. ROOT CAUSE
=============
Accepted at: ui/src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.tsx:AtsIntegrationSectionView
— handleCcEmailAddressesChange copies the raw input string into
sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses.
Validated at:
ui/src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.tsx:handleCcEmailAddressesBlur
— the field is split on both semicolons and commas, trimmed, empties removed, and then rejoined
with commas; it does not preserve the original semicolon separator.
Transformed at:
ui/src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.tsx:handleCcEmailAddressesBlur

— semicolon-separated input is explicitly transformed into a comma-separated string.
Stored at: accounts-service/src/main/resources/graphql/
settings.graphqls:AtsIntegrationSettingsInput.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses
— the field is accepted as a plain String; the persistence implementation is not shown in the
evidence, so no backend normalization is verified there.
Consumed at: candidate-service/src/main/kotlin/com/asurint/candidate/handlers/commands/
SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.kt:validateEmails
— downstream parsing splits on both semicolons and commas, so it can read either representation.
Confirmed: The UI is the verified source of the semicolon-to-comma conversion —
ui/src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.tsx:handleCcEmailAddressesBlur
rejoins parsed emails with ",".
Confirmed: Downstream email sending is not dependent on commas specifically —
candidate-service/src/main/kotlin/com/asurint/candidate/handlers/commands/
SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.kt:validateEmails
accepts both ";" and "," delimiters.
Hypothesis: accounts-service persists whatever string the UI submits for
sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses —
accounts-service/src/main/resources/graphql/
settings.graphqls:AtsIntegrationSettingsInput.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses
defines the field as String, but the resolver/entity code that writes it was not shown.
Unknown: Which accounts-service resolver/entity performs the actual assignment for
AtsIntegrationSettings.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses — inspecting the mutation resolver
and persistence mapper for settings updates would confirm whether any backend normalization also
occurs.
Not the cause: Candidate Submitted Notifications display behavior —
ui/src/apps/client/modules/Settings/pages/ApplicationSettings/components/
ReportEventsCCEmailAddressSettings.tsx::ReportEventsCCEmailAddressSettings
only renders ccEmailAddresses as provided and shows no delimiter conversion logic.

4. PROPOSED SOLUTION
====================
Update the ATS integration settings UI so the 'Enable Link to user placing order' CC Email Addresses
field trims and de-duplicates separators without converting semicolons to commas, preserving
semicolon-separated values through save and reload. Keep accounts-service schema unchanged because
the field is already a String, but verify persistence code does not add its own normalization
before implementation. Leave candidate-service parsing logic unchanged because
SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.validateEmails already accepts both semicolon- and comma-separated
stored values, which preserves readability of existing comma-separated records.

result with commas before calling atsIntegrationChange.
Change: Modify ATS integration CC email blur normalization so this field preserves semicolon
separators by rejoining cleaned entries with semicolons instead of commas.
How: Reuse the existing blur normalization path in handleCcEmailAddressesBlur rather than adding
a second save-time transform. Keep the current trimming and empty-entry removal, but change
the delimiter handling for this field so semicolon-separated input stays semicolon-separated
after atsIntegrationChange. New tests are required because no existing test file sits beside
this symbol; add them at
src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.test.tsx.
Why: The reported conversion is directly implemented here:
ui/src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/
view.tsx::handleCcEmailAddressesBlur
rejoins with commas. Changing this symbol fixes the verified source of the bad stored value
for this field only.
Sketch:
const trimmed = (atsIntegration.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses ?? "")
.split(/;+/)
.map((email) => email.trim())
.filter((email) => email.length > 0)
.join(";");
atsIntegrationChange({
sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses: trimmed,
});
Done when:
- Entering 'alpha@example.com;beta@example.com;gamma@example.com' and blurring the field
updates sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses to
'alpha@example.com;beta@example.com;gamma@example.com'.
- Entering ' alpha@example.com ; beta@example.com ;; gamma@example.com ' and blurring the
field updates sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses to
'alpha@example.com;beta@example.com;gamma@example.com'.
- If the loaded value is 'old1@example.com,old2@example.com' and the field is not edited, the
UI continues to display that comma-separated string unchanged on reload.
Impact Analysis (Change 1):
Risk: Medium
Summary: The code change is small and local to the blur handler, but it alters the stored format
of sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses, which accounts-service stores (persistence code not
inspected) and candidate-service reads.
Direct Impact:
- ui::AtsIntegrationSectionView (view.tsx): renders the field and registers
handleCcEmailAddressesBlur as its blur handler, so every edit of the field passes through the
changed code.
- ui::atsIntegrationChange: receives the rejoined string and updates the settings form state, so
the delimiter produced here is what gets saved.
Potential Impact:
- ui::SettingsForm (depth 2): submits the form state on save, so the semicolon-separated value
reaches the API.
- accounts-service::AtsIntegrationSettingsInput.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses (depth
3): stored as a plain String; the persistence code was not provided, so hidden normalization
cannot be ruled out.
- candidate-service::SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.validateEmails (depth 4): reads the stored
value and splits on [;,]+, so it accepts both separators.

9. ARCHITECTURE
===============
The fix stays on the existing settings flow: preserve the delimiter at the UI entry point, keep
storage as an opaque string, and rely on the existing downstream parser that already accepts both
delimiter styles.

10. TESTING
===========
The key regression is that the current UI blur logic converts semicolons to commas. Because no
existing test file sits beside AtsIntegrationSectionView, the required automated coverage must be
added in the new test file path provided with that symbol.
- [regression] TO ADD: In ui AtsIntegrationSectionView, enter
'qa1@example.com;qa2@example.com;qa3@example.com' into sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses and
blur the field; today the blur handler emits 'qa1@example.com,qa2@example.com,qa3@example.com',
after the fix it must emit 'qa1@example.com;qa2@example.com;qa3@example.com'.
Expected: The test fails against the current comma-joining implementation and passes after
handleCcEmailAddressesBlur rejoins with semicolons.
- [unit] TO ADD: In ui AtsIntegrationSectionView, enter ' alpha@example.com ; beta@example.com ;;
gamma@example.com ' and blur the field.
Expected: atsIntegrationChange receives sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses equal to
'alpha@example.com;beta@example.com;gamma@example.com'.
- [edge_case] TO ADD: In ui AtsIntegrationSectionView, start with an empty
sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses value and blur without entering any emails.
Expected: atsIntegrationChange receives an empty string and no commas or semicolons are
introduced.
- [regression] TO ADD: Render ui AtsIntegrationSectionView with an existing stored value
'old1@example.com,old2@example.com' and do not edit the field.
Expected: The input displays 'old1@example.com,old2@example.com' unchanged, confirming legacy
comma-separated values remain readable until edited.
- [integration] EXISTING behavior to run after UI fix: candidate-service
SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.handle processes clientCCNotificationsEmails set to
'one@example.com;two@example.com;three@example.com'.
Expected: validateEmails splits the string into three email addresses and email publishing still
works with semicolon-separated storage.
- [integration] EXISTING behavior to run after UI fix: candidate-service
SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.handle processes clientCCNotificationsEmails set to
'old1@example.com,old2@example.com'.
Expected: validateEmails splits the string into two email addresses and legacy comma-separated
storage remains readable.

2. Add proposed test file ui
src/common/accounts/client/components/SettingsForm/sections/AtsIntegrationSection/view.test.tsx
for handleCcEmailAddressesBlur covering semicolon preservation, whitespace/duplicate separator
cleanup, empty input, and unchanged rendering of a preloaded comma-separated value; this is

3, and 4.

AtsIntegrationSettingsInput.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses and the corresponding settings
mutation implementation to confirm no backend normalization rewrites the string before
persistence; if the implementation writes the raw String unchanged, no code edit is needed, and
this check supports the end-to-end save/reload behavior described in testing_plan scenario 4.
4. Run existing candidate-service coverage around
src/main/kotlin/com/asurint/candidate/handlers/commands/SendDirectRequestEmailHandler.kt
validateEmails to confirm both semicolon-separated and comma-separated clientCCNotificationsEmails
remain accepted after the UI change; this guards backward compatibility and maps to testing_plan
scenarios 5 and 6.

12. RISKS
=========
- The actual accounts-service resolver/entity that persists
AtsIntegrationSettings.sendReportRequestedLinkCcEmailAddresses was not provided; if it also
normalizes delimiters, the UI-only code change will not fully fix save/reload behavior.
- Editing a legacy comma-separated value and saving after the UI fix will normalize it to
semicolon-separated format for this field; this matches the ticket intent but changes
representation on first edit.

14. OTHER NOTES
===============
Error handling: Current UI blur handling removes empty tokens and trims whitespace but rewrites
delimiters to commas. The proposed UI change keeps the same empty-token cleanup while preserving
semicolons for this field. candidate-service currently tolerates both semicolon and comma
delimiters when sending emails; no new backend error handling is required by the evidence.
Security: This change affects only formatting and storage of a CC email string field. No
authentication, authorization, or sensitive-data handling changes are evidenced in the provided
material.
Backward compatibility: No API schema change is proposed. Existing comma-separated stored values
remain readable because candidate-service already parses both delimiters, and the UI should

continue to display legacy comma-separated values unchanged until the field is edited and saved
again.
